chapter: Vaudeville and the name Mac and Mac
title: How they became Mac and Mac
summary: In Atlanta in 1911, producer George Freeman at the Paradise Theater shortened their billing from Mac Bride and Mac Bride to Mac and Mac.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: And we could always stay as long as we'd want. Usually we'd always get three or four weeks by being able to change our act. And those Northern acts, we called them Northern acts because they all turned their noses up at us at first, you know, when they saw it. But what a riot we were when we finished our act. Then they come in to try to be friends. And so they used to come around and pat you on the back there and tell you, I'll find you, oh, I really enjoyed your act. And once in 1911, that was right after the comet, Halley's Comet, we were in Atlanta.

And this is where we got the Mac and Mac from. We were at Bailey's and their builders is Mac Bride and Mac Bride, you know. But there was a man named George Freeman that was producing shows over on Peter Street in Atlanta. At a theater called the Paradise Theater. And when we went over there to work, he said, now, I'm going to have to change your billing. See, I tried to get that Mac Bride and Mac Bride, but that's too long. See, why not just call yourself Mac and Mac? Well, that's where it started. So George Freeman was the one that gave us that. Yeah. Good stuff.
